articles.title: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
articles.raw_description: Instead of YouTube, watch HackerTube! HackerTube 31 Oct, 2026 It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org ! Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews, filtered them down, ran Sonnet over them in a workflow, got rid of spam and low grade content, and narrowed them down to just 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics. Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila! HackerTube: Contains quality content Uses the 50% thumbnail instead of the uploaded thumbnail Custom and good ForYou recommendations without any user accounts, storing state in local browser session Keyboard shortcuts Export of the site's data available to give to your agent to easily create your own version This takes ~2 hours now. I can breathe again. Thank you Opus 5.5 <3.
articles.summary: HackerTubeは、Hacker Newsで推薦されたYouTube動画のみを集めたYouTubeクローンです。AI（Opus 5.5）がHacker Newsのコメントを分析し、スパムや低品質なコンテンツを除外して推薦動画を抽出しました。これにより、過度に誇張されたサムネイルや質の低いコンテンツにうんざりしていた開発者が、より質の高い動画視聴体験を求めて開発したものです。アカウント不要でローカルストレージに状態を保存し、サイトデータのエクスポート機能も備えています。

articles.title: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8
articles.raw_description: CVE-2026-98432 is a CVSS 9.8 remote use-after-free in Linux's IPv4 TCP handshake, fixed upstream Oct 15. Ubuntu and RHEL haven't shipped a fixed kernel yet. # Overview Linux's stable kernels shipped a fix on October 11 and 15, 2026 for CVE-2026-98432 , a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake that a remote, unauthenticated peer can reach. The kernel's own CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8, Critical . The fixed releases are 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 , and 7.3 , and the bug goes back to Linux 4.4. The upstream fix is a four-line change, but most servers run a distribution's kernel, and as of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31, Ubuntu's tracker still reads "Vulnerable" for its kernel on every release, and Red Hat, which now rates the bug Critical too, lists RHEL 8, 9, and 10 as affected with no fix. Why it's urgent: the bug sits in code every Linux server runs when it accepts an IPv4 TCP connection, before any application sees the connection. Anthropic, whose researcher reported it, says its Claude model wrote a working proof-of-concept exploit that runs commands as root on "Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener," with no credentials. Go programs open those listeners by default, per the Go Security Team. See the timeline . # Key facts Field Detail CVE CVE-2026-98432, "ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period," issued by the Linux kernel CNA Severity Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8 ( AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:
articles.summary: LinuxカーネルのIPv4 TCPハンドシェイク処理において、リモートから認証なしで攻撃可能なUse-After-Freeの脆弱性（CVE-2026-98432）が発見されました。この脆弱性はCVSS 9.8と評価されており、攻撃者はroot権限でコマンドを実行できる可能性があります。修正はアップストリームで提供されていますが、UbuntuやRHELなどの主要ディストリビューションではまだ修正版カーネルがリリースされておらず、多くのLinuxサーバーが影響を受ける可能性があります。

articles.title: It's the memory latency, stupid
articles.raw_description: When your database CPU is at 100%, what is it actually doing? Memory stalls, CPU caches, and how radix partitioning makes GROUP BY faster. â All posts When you see your databases CPU at 100%, what is it actually doing? We like to act as though CPUs run code linearly for simplicity's sake, but in truth CPUs are incredibly complex beasts; they can potentially do many instructions at once, or sometimes none at all (despite our console showing 100%). Because CPUs can do so many things, one CPU at 100% may be doing much less than another at 100%. A CPU is considered "idle" only if no task (Linux task) needs CPU time; this does not mean the CPU itself is being fully saturated. So why would a CPU not be fully utilized, even if it appears to be at 100%? The answer is usually memory . Memory accesses are orders of magnitude slower than internal CPU operations. To give a good picture of how much so, a modern CPU might be able to process somewhere in the realm of 4-8 instructions per nanosecond. A memory access to RAM can take somewhere in the realm of 50-100ns. To ease your mathing, that means a modern CPU can do around 400-800 instructions for every one memory access from RAM. articles.summary: データベースのCPU使用率が100%に達しても、CPUが常に命令を実行しているわけではありません。CPUは命令を並列実行できる一方、メモリへのアクセス速度はCPUの処理速度に比べて非常に遅いため、CPUがメモリ待ちでアイドル状態になることがあります。このメモリレイテンシがCPUの真の利用率を低下させる主な原因です。

articles.title: An Italian farmer found some unknown seeds in his attic and planted them
articles.raw_description: When a seven-eared stem emerged from the ground, it seemed like a miracle. What Claudio Grossi had unearthed was an ancient grain that proved to be an answer to some modern problems At his farm near Parma, Italy, Claudio Grossi offers a visual history of his miracle grain in photos, crackers and loaves. Clara Vannucci Sometime in the early 1990s, Claudio Grossi, a 40-year-old farmer in Parma, in northern Italy, was cleaning his attic when he turned up an old sack full of seeds that he couldn’t identify. The bag, he was sure, had been left by his late great-grandfather, who’d started the farmstead around 1915. Grossi had no idea how long the seeds had been sitting there, deprived of water, soil and sun. Dry and cracked, the kernels looked so old in the palm of his hand that he doubted anything would ever sprout from them. He carried the bag down the stairs, shook the seeds out into a pile of manure and then forgot about them. To his surprise, the seeds soon sprouted a few different types of wheat. One was particularly striking: At six feet high, its plants were about twice as tall as commercial wheat. But the most remarkable feature came when it developed ears—the grain-studded parts at the top of the plant. All of the wheat types Grossi had previously seen grew only one such ear. articles.title: Memdoor: A team of 5 Qwen3.8-27B models beats Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
articles.raw_description: A lightweight coding and automation agent in one CLI binary. Run locally or over SSH, optimize token use, and automate CI and cron with durable workflows. - guregodevo/memdoor team-solve A multi-agent harness for programming problems, written as a Memdoor workflow. Five roles (planner, two ideators, solver, manager) and a repair worker each start from a fresh context and talk only through files on disk. A shell script that runs the samples decides success, not a model. It is the method of GVS5H (Lee, 2026: five Qwen3.8-27B models match Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard). Rebuilt with the authors' exact prompts on Qwen3.8-27B, their loop scored a mean of 9.8 of 10 over five passes on the first ten LiveCodeBench Hard problems, against 9.6 for their own harness and 8.0 for Fable 5 alone ( below , every run published). The coder wrote these files itself from a description of the method (2026-10-25). Nobody hand-wrote them. Five passes on the authors' ten (2026-10-31) GVS5H's own harness, rebuilt as a Memdoor workflow on the same model: Qwen3.8-27B, a 128K reply cap, the authors' prompts and loop. articles.summary: Memdoorは、5つのQwen3.8-27Bモデルを使用したマルチエージェントシステムで、LiveCodeBench Hardのコーディング問題においてFable 5を上回る性能を示しました。このシステムは、プランナー、アイデア創出者、ソルバー、マネージャー、リペアワーカーといった役割を持つエージェントがファイルを通じてのみ通信し、シェルスクリプトによって成功が判定されます。Qwen3.8-27Bモデルと著者指定のプロンプト、ループ構造を用いることで、平均9.8/10のスコアを達成し、これはFable 5単体（平均8.0/10）よりも優れています。このアプローチは、コーディングと自動化エージェントを単一のCLIバイナリに統合し、ローカルまたはSSH経由で実行可能で、トークン使用量の最適化やCI/cronの自動化を目的としています。

articles.title: First response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite
articles.raw_description: This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit. We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite. Travis Beals Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence Oct 30, 2026 On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher. The launch marked the first step in our long-term research moonshot to explore powering AI compute in space. Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests. This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit. During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Following this initial output, we tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts reporting the technical status of the payload systems. Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027. Our chips have officially earn
articles.summary: Project Suncatcherのプロトタイプ衛星が、軌道上でデータセンタークラスのTPU（Tensor Processing Unit）を使用した初のAI応答を達成した。衛星に搭載されたGemma 4モデルに宇宙に関する俳句生成を指示し、成功裏に実行された。この成果は、宇宙空間でのAIコンピューティングの電力供給を探求する長期研究の一環であり、今後の熱ストレスや放射線被曝下でのTPU性能評価、そして2027年の双子衛星ミッションへと繋がる重要な一歩である。

articles.title: Altoids Project
articles.raw_description: My 12-year-old son and I spent about two months on, what we call, the Altoids project. Here is the final product (video): My 12-year-old son and I spent about two months on, what we call, the Altoids project. Here is the final product ( video ): It all started when I took him to MIT Swapfest for the first time. We saw an assembled robot from a couple’s booth; later we learned that it was from a kit . It was built by their daughter many years ago. After realizing I had come with my son, they gave us the robot for free. We also picked up a used ThinkPad laptop at a very reasonable price, which we used for the project. As any curious mind would, we disassembled the robot. Noticing that we were missing the control, we wanted to see which parts we could reuse. We took the 128x64 display off. But we couldn’t find the pinout for the display. We tried using AI, but it hallucinated so badly that it gave us a 20-pin pinout when the display only has 10 pins. After hours of searching around, we found the exact schematic posted on Arduino’s forum by a stranger on the Internet. God bless him. With the pinout, we finally made the display show something. We ran the Space Trash game from the U8g2 library . Let’s call this v1. I had just watched a YouTube video where someone built a tiny computer and fit everything inside an Altoids tin ( video ). articles.summary: 12歳の息子と共に、MIT Swapfestで入手したロボットキットの部品を再利用して、Altoids缶に収まる小型コンピュータを製作したプロジェクトの記録。特に、ロボットから取り外した128x64ディスプレイのピンアウト情報を見つけるのに苦労し、AIの誤情報に翻弄された末、Arduinoフォーラムで偶然見つけた情報によって表示に成功した。その後、YouTubeの動画に触発され、Altoids缶への小型化を試みた。
